inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026 pro-forma CONTINUING portfolio on South32's proportional-consolidation (Underlying) basis: Sierra Gorda 1,154 + Cannington 852 + Australia Manganese 675 + South Africa Manganese 364 (AR FY26 operations table, p39). Excludes the aluminium value chain being sold to Alcoa (4,498 of FY26 underlying revenue), Mozal (890; care & maintenance since Mar-2026, retained but valued at nil), Cerro Matoso (divested Dec-2025) and third-party products. Statutory revenue of 5,816 equity-accounts Sierra Gorda and manganese and is NOT the base for the 2,462 Underlying EBITDA, which is proportional; the two bases must not be mixed.
inputs.share_count_basis: 4,486m ordinary shares on issue at 30-Jun-2026 (AR FY26 p22) plus ~14m unvested share rights, ~4,500m fully diluted (FY26 diluted EPS denominator 4,503m weighted). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; the on-market buyback (US$35m FY26, US$209m remaining to Sep-2027) funds the flat count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Ex-lease: cash 2,134 less other interest-bearing liabilities 1,103 = net cash 1,031 (AR FY26 balance sheet table p33). Company-defined net cash is 283 because it also nets lease liabilities of 748; those are charged in the flows instead (lease treatment B). Group cash only; EAI cash and Sierra Gorda's own balance sheet are inside the proportional flows.
inputs.sbc_source: AR FY26 cash flow statement share-based payments add-back (US$20m); no equity-award withholding tax disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0). Interest income stripped is the US$67m 'interest income on cash and cash equivalents' (AR FY26 note, line 2131), NOT the US$487m 'interest received', which is dominated by the US$401m accrued-interest distribution on the Sierra Gorda shareholder loan; that loan and its interest are eliminated on the proportional basis the flows are built on.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Whole-group FY26 owner FCF for the record: reported FCF 540 (OCF 1,634 - capex 1,094, statutory, includes 503 of EAI net distributions) - SBC 20 - cash interest 67 = 453. The forward flows are NOT anchored to this number: they are rebuilt from the pro-forma continuing revenue base above, because ~55% of FY26 revenue is being sold.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in USD; ASX quote in AUD. fx_rate is USD->AUD = 1/0.7016 = 1.4253 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X 0.7016 at 2026-09-25T04:32Z). Parity check: A$4.94 x 0.7016 = US$3.466 vs SOUHY ADR US$17.36 / 5 shares = US$3.472 (0.2% tie, 2026-09-24 close) and S32.L 259.6p. Unsuffixed per-share values are in AUD (quote currency); USD twins are the model currency.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the flows' currency: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.15 = ~10% cost of equity; net cash, so WACC = cost of equity = 10.0%. No cyclical or execution premium is stacked on top: commodity-price risk is charged in the flows (mid-cycle deck, 30% bear weight) and Hermosa execution risk in the bear path. One WACC across all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. FY26 lease cash = principal 110 + interest 59 = 169 (2.1% of 8,108 underlying revenue); pro-forma continuing share set at 3.0% of revenue (Hermosa alone carries ~US$60m/yr of self-generated-power leases excluded from its capex guidance). Lease liabilities (748) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation.
inputs.nci_treatment: Sierra Gorda (45%) and Samancor manganese (60%) are equity-accounted; the flows use South32's proportional share so they are attributable by construction. Consolidated NCI is US$14m (Mozal minority) - immaterial, ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical') on a PRO-FORMA basis with mid-cycle commodity normalisation. Why pro-forma: on 30-Jun-2026 South32 agreed to sell Worsley, Hillside, Brazil Alumina/Aluminium and MRN to Alcoa (US$3,100m cash + 17m Alcoa shares + up to US$750m price-linked contingent, locked box at 31-Mar-2026, completion H2 FY27). Under the locked box the aluminium chain's post-March-2026 cash accrues to Alcoa, so it is valued as a bridge item at risk-adjusted consideration, not projected. Why mid-cycle: FY26 realised prices (Cu US$5.92/lb, Ag US$66-71/oz, Zn US$3,000/t) and the FY27 guidance deck (Cu 6.20, Ag 65, Zn 3,500, Mn 4.90) are cycle highs; base reverts to Cu 4.75 / Ag 35 / Zn 2,800 / Pb 2,000 / Mn 4.50 by FY28, with FY27 a 50/50 blend. Volumes follow guidance: Sierra Gorda CuEq 91.8kt FY27 / 94.0kt FY28 and +30% from FY31 (fourth grinding line, FID 30-Jun-2026, South32 share of capex ~US$326m FY27-30); Cannington 290kt ZnEq FY27-28 (+41% vs FY26 205.4kt, low-grade stockpile milling); Australia Manganese 2,650-2,900kwmt (vs 3,598 sold in FY26 restart year); Taylor first production H2 FY28, full capacity FY31, steady-state revenue ~US$1,000m / EBITDA ~US$550m at the mid-cycle deck (company: ~US$650m at its deck), growth capex US$3.3B of which ~US$2.7B spent/guided through FY27. Functional cost saving of US$125m/yr fully realised FY29 is in the group-cost line (~110/yr net incl. greenfield exploration and Mozal holding cost). Rehabilitation provisions on retained assets are not deducted (folder convention) - a known omission, ~US$0.5-0.8B undiscounted for Cannington/manganese/Sierra Gorda share. Historical CAGRs describe a portfolio that will not exist and are reported for the record only.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year pro-forma revenue CAGR (3,045 -> ~4,530 by FY36: Taylor + Sierra Gorda 4th line on a mid-cycle deck); historical CAGRs are not used
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All CAGRs describe a portfolio that will not exist after H2 FY27: Illawarra Coal (Aug-2024), Cerro Matoso (Dec-2025) and the aluminium chain (~55% of FY26 underlying revenue) are gone. EPS CAGRs are undefined (FY21 and FY23 EPS negative). Owner-FCF series: FY16 580, FY17 1,735, FY18 1,177, FY19 998, FY20 547, FY21 781, FY22 2,422, FY23 195, FY24 -68, FY25 286, FY26 453 - a commodity cycle, not a growth trend.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - cash interest, applied across the full history. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR of +32% is trough-to-recovery (FY23 base of 195 after the FY22 peak of 2,422) and means nothing; the 5yr -10% is the honest read of a business whose reported FCF has been sustained by asset sales and EAI distributions while growth capex (Hermosa 711 in FY26) consumes it.

base.growth_note: FY27 3,050 (50/50 blend of the FY27 guidance deck ~3,383 and mid-cycle ~2,710); FY28 2,760 (mid-cycle 2,710 + Taylor first ore 50); FY29 3,060 (Taylor 350); FY30 3,410 (Taylor 700); FY31 4,000 (Taylor 1,000 + Sierra Gorda 4th line +290); then 2.5% nominal. Cannington assumed extended past FY33 (28% reserve uplift, extension studies live).
base.margin_note: Mid-cycle continuing EBITDA ~966 on 2,710 = 35.6% (SG 546, Cannington 409, AusMn 150, SAMn 16, Hermosa pre-production -45, group/exploration/Mozal -110). FY27 blend 40.5%. Taylor at ~55% and the 4th line at ~65% incremental lift the mature margin to 43.5%.
base.capex_note: FY27 = guidance 1,500 incl. EAIs + 80 capitalised exploration = 1,580. FY28 1,130 (Hermosa ~550 tail of the US$3.3B), FY29 750, FY30 690, then sustaining ~620 rising with revenue (SG 230, Cannington 80, manganese 100, Taylor 100, exploration 80, intangibles ~15) = 15.5%.
base.tax_note: Underlying ETR 34% (AU 30% + royalty-related taxes, Chile 27% + mining royalty, US 21%+AZ). Cash rate dips FY29-30 as Taylor's US$3.3B tax depreciation starts; 33% mature.
base.narrative: Prices revert to mid-cycle by FY28; Taylor delivered on the April-2026 revised schedule and budget; the Alcoa sale completes in H2 FY27 at the headline terms.

bull.growth_note: FY27 at the full guidance deck (3,383); structural-deficit deck thereafter: Cu US$5.50/lb, Ag US$50/oz, Zn US$3,200/t, Mn US$5.00/dmtu -> continuing 3,143; Taylor ramps 60/400/800/1,150 (de-bottlenecked above nameplate via the Clark decline); 4th line +340 FY31; 3% nominal thereafter.
bull.narrative: Electrification/AI demand keeps copper and silver near current levels; Taylor arrives on schedule and de-bottlenecks above design; the 4th grinding line and Cannington open-pit extension are delivered; the market re-rates the simplified base-metals portfolio.

bear.growth_note: Trough deck from FY28: Cu US$3.90/lb, Ag US$26/oz, Zn US$2,500/t, Mn US$4.00/dmtu -> continuing 2,328 (SAMn loss-making at that deck). Taylor slips a further year (first production FY30, full FY32) with another ~US$500m overrun; 4th line delayed to FY33; Cannington NOT extended and closes end-FY33 (-20% revenue in FY34).
bear.narrative: China-led demand slowdown takes copper and silver back to 2023-24 levels while Taylor - already +US$1.1B and a year late - slips again; South32 funds the overrun from the Alcoa proceeds in a price trough, manganese runs at breakeven, and Cannington's FY33 closure is not replaced.

scenario_narratives.base: The company that exists after H2 FY27 is a 45% Sierra Gorda stake, Cannington, a 60%/54.6% manganese business and a US$3.3B zinc-lead-silver mine under construction, plus ~US$3.7B of risk-adjusted Alcoa proceeds and US$1.0B of net cash. Base assumes prices revert from the FY26/FY27 highs (Cu US$5.92-6.20/lb, Ag US$65-71/oz) to a mid-cycle deck (Cu 4.75, Ag 35, Zn 2,800, Mn 4.50) by FY28, which takes continuing EBITDA from ~1,430 (FY26 actual) to ~970. Owner FCF is negative in FY27 (~-670) and FY28 (~-370) while Hermosa consumes US$1,000m then ~550m, turns positive in FY29 and reaches ~630 in FY31 once Taylor (~US$1,000m revenue, ~55% margin at the mid-cycle deck) and the Sierra Gorda fourth grinding line (+30% CuEq) are at capacity. The axes are the price deck and Taylor delivery; the Alcoa package is worth ~A$1.16/share on its own.
scenario_narratives.bull: Copper and silver hold near current levels on the structural-deficit thesis (Cu 5.50, Ag 50), FY27 lands at the full guidance deck, Taylor is on the April-2026 schedule and de-bottlenecks ~25% above design via the Clark decline, the fourth grinding line delivers FY31 and Cannington's open-pit extension replaces the FY33 underground closure. Mature margin 47%, terminal cap 14x. Even here the FY27-28 Hermosa spend keeps cumulative owner FCF negative until FY29.
scenario_narratives.bear: A demand-led price reversion to 2023-24 levels (Cu 3.90, Ag 26, Zn 2,500) coincides with a second Taylor slip and overrun; South32 spends ~US$2.4B of cumulative negative owner FCF over FY27-31 funded by the Alcoa cash, South Africa Manganese is loss-making at the deck, and Cannington closes in FY33 without replacement. The DCF of the continuing business is negative and the equity is essentially the Alcoa proceeds, net cash and the Illawarra receivable, less the Hermosa burn.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: realised prices are at multi-decade highs (silver US$66-71/oz vs a ten-year average near US$24; copper US$5.92 vs ~US$3.80) so the reversion risk is asymmetric, and the flagship project has already had one +50% capex overrun and a schedule slip. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things - the deck holding, Taylor on the revised schedule and the fourth line/Cannington extension - all to land. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the business that will exist, at the prices that persist. South32 post-Alcoa is a US$3.7B cash-and-shares receivable, US$1.0B of net cash, two high-margin base-metals assets it does not fully own or operate, a marginal manganese business and a US$3.3B construction project. The market price (A$4.94, ~US$15.6B) implies an enterprise value of ~US$11B for the continuing operations, which is ~7x FY26 EBITDA at cycle-high prices but ~11x mid-cycle and ~6x the FY31 EBITDA that requires Taylor and the fourth line to arrive. The house view charges the price cycle in the flows: base reverts to mid-cycle, the bear takes 30% weight. Each +US$0.50/lb sustained copper is worth ~A$0.26/share and each +US$10/oz silver ~A$0.64/share; the current price is consistent with a permanent deck near Cu US$5.50-6.00 / Ag US$55-65, which the house does not underwrite.
key_risks_to_valuation: Price deck: the entire gap to the market price is the deck. Sustained copper above US$5.50/lb and silver above US$50/oz would put the base near the current price.
Hermosa/Taylor execution: capex already +US$1.1B to US$3.3B, first production moved to H2 FY28; another slip in a price trough is the bear case and it consumes most of the Alcoa proceeds.

Alcoa completion: shareholder vote and FIRB/Brazil/SA approvals; consideration includes 17m Alcoa shares (equity-market exposure) and US$750m price-linked contingent (taken at 20%). Disposal tax (assumed US$300m) is undisclosed.
Non-operated assets: Sierra Gorda (45%, KGHM operates) and Ambler (50%) control capital timing and costs; the fourth grinding line is a JV decision.
Cannington reserve life to FY33; base assumes extension, bear does not.

Rehabilitation/closure provisions on retained assets are not deducted (folder convention); Alcoa assumes ~US$1.1-1.2B of the aluminium chain's provisions, which is part of why the EV looks higher than the cash.
USD/AUD: the flows are USD, the quote is AUD; a stronger AUD lowers the AUD value per share one-for-one.
